component: STM32G474 candidate MCU (VBAT/RTC retention domain, FDCAN, safe-state outputs)
failure_mode: Core/flash/SRAM fault: corrupted program flow or state (wrong torque/contactor command or loss of the safe-state reaction)
sm_spf: External windowed watchdog + NRST-driven safe state (SSN-owned)
sm_latent: Reset-cause and retention-record check at boot; safe-state frame 0x100 consumed by SSN (SafetyManual sec. 4.1)
note: T0 assumption: 40 percent of the MCU base rate lands in core/memory; DC 90 percent = ISO 26262-5 Annex D medium class for a windowed watchdog with program-flow monitoring; latent DC 90 percent because a watchdog reset is recorded and reported at the next boot. Vendor FMEDA replaces the fraction and the coverage at H-02.

component: STM32G474 candidate MCU (VBAT/RTC retention domain, FDCAN, safe-state outputs)
failure_mode: VBAT/RTC retention domain fault: backup registers corrupted or backup-domain switch failure (stale or invalid retention record)
sm_spf: Retention-record CRC and version check (SW-FR-LOG-004); invalid record -> safe state
sm_latent: Boot-time record validation reports the invalid record (diagnostic frame)
note: T0 assumption: 10 percent of the MCU rate in the backup domain; CRC-protected record gives high coverage (Annex D high class 99 percent) against both wrong-content and detection-at-boot; a corrupted record that passes CRC is the residual.

component: STM32G474 candidate MCU (VBAT/RTC retention domain, FDCAN, safe-state outputs)
failure_mode: GPIO/output-stage fault: safe-state or contactor-enable output stuck in the active (non-safe) state
note: Single-point fault: the HwRS v0.3.0 defines no output read-back or independent second path for the safe-state outputs, so no diagnostic coverage is claimed. Dominant SPFM contributor; see docs/hw/fmeda.md finding FMEDA-F-001.

component: STM32G474 candidate MCU (VBAT/RTC retention domain, FDCAN, safe-state outputs)
failure_mode: FDCAN peripheral fault: corrupted or mistimed frame content (wrong torque/safe-state message on the bus)
sm_spf: ISO 11898-1 CRC/format checks and protocol error counters; bus-off -> receiver safe state
sm_latent: Error counters / bus-off reported in diagnostics; receiver time-out reaction
note: T0 assumption: 20 percent of the MCU rate in the CAN peripheral; the CAN protocol layer detects corrupted frames with high coverage (Annex D high class 99 percent); latent coverage 90 percent via error counters. A message that is well-formed but wrong in content is the residual.

component: STM32G474 candidate MCU (VBAT/RTC retention domain, FDCAN, safe-state outputs)
failure_mode: Faults of peripherals not used by the safety function (ADC, timers, USB, unused ports)
note: Safe fault: no effect on the safety goal and no safety-mechanism role; kept safety-related so it stays inside the SPFM/LFM denominators (conservative, ISO 26262-5 Annex C.7/C.8).

component: SPEC-HF009-10UF hold-up capacitor (VBAT retention energy store)
failure_mode: Open circuit / loss of capacitance (no hold-up energy during a supply drop)
sm_latent: Retention record missing/invalid after a supply event is detected by the boot-time record check
note: The hold-up capacitor is a safety mechanism for HW-SF-002 (retention through a 150 ms supply drop); its failure cannot violate the safety goal alone but removes the retention protection: multiple-point fault. Latent DC 90 percent because loss of the record is perceived at the next boot; T0 assumption on the failure-mode distribution.

component: SPEC-HF009-10UF hold-up capacitor (VBAT retention energy store)
failure_mode: Short circuit (VBAT domain pulled down; retention domain lost)
sm_latent: Backup-domain reset flag / invalid record at boot
note: Multiple-point fault as for FMEDA-006; a hard short discharges the retention domain and is perceived as a backup-domain reset at the next boot (DC 90 percent, T0 assumption).

component: SPEC-HF009-10UF hold-up capacitor (VBAT retention energy store)
failure_mode: Parametric drift (capacitance or leakage out of the C_eff / I_leak budget)
note: Multiple-point fault with no detection: a degraded but not failed capacitor still covers short events and is only exposed by a long supply drop; latent until then. Candidate for a periodic hold-up self-test at H-02 (finding FMEDA-F-002).
